name: Lancaster University

settingEvidence.evidence: The Lancaster University campus occupies a beautiful 578-acre parkland site at Bailrigg, just three miles from Lancaster city centre.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK (Home) students in 2027/28; a placement year costs 20% and a study abroad year 15% of the standard fee

source.evidence: Our Undergraduate Tuition Fees for 2027/28 are: ... Home ... £10,050 ... Students studying abroad for a year: 15% of the standard tuition fee ... Students taking a work placement for a year: 20% of the standard tuition fee

livingCosts.text: On-campus undergraduate rooms cost about £149-£278 a week in 2026/27 (contracts generally run for 40 weeks). Self-catered single rooms start at £148.89 with a shared bathroom; catered en suite rooms, which include meals, are £276.29-£278.05

source.evidence: Our contracts generally run for 40 weeks. ... Prices apply to the 2026/27 academic year. ... £148.89 ... £276.29-£278.05

openDays.text: The only undergraduate open day listed, Saturday 17 October 2026, has already passed and no later dates are published yet. In-person and live-streamed campus tours run throughout the year.

source.evidence: Undergraduate open day, Saturday 17 October 2026 ... In-person and live-streamed campus tours are available throughout the year.

contextual.summary: Lancaster's Contextual Offer Scheme gives UK applicants who had free school meals or have experience of care an offer typically two A level grades lower, and completing the Lancaster Access Programme can lower it by up to three grades.
contextual.typicalReduction: Typically two A level grades lower than the standard offer (for example AAB becomes BBB); up to three grades lower after completing the Lancaster Access Programme

criteria.detail: Received Free School Meals during secondary education, as declared on your UCAS application

Successfully completing the Lancaster Access Programme (Year 12 and 13) typically earns an alternative offer up to three A level grades lower; to join you must meet two or more widening participation criteria

contextual.rulesText: For 2026 entry, UK students get the lower offer if they received Free School Meals during secondary education (as declared on UCAS) or have experience of being in care. There is no separate application. You can combine it with the Lancaster Access Programme and receive whichever offer is better for you.

source.evidence: we will take into account additional contextual information when reviewing applications from UK students, if either: ... You have received Free School Meals during your secondary education, as declared on the UCAS application ... You have experience of being in care

programmes.name: Lancaster Access Programme
programmes.summary: A free supported-entry programme for Year 12 and 13 students from widening participation backgrounds, with events, online workshops and 3-day residentials on campus; finishing it typically earns a lower offer at Lancaster.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 or 13 students at a UK state school or college who are predicted at least BBC at A-level, have five GCSEs at grade 4 or above including English Language and Maths, and meet two or more widening participation criteria.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Attend a UK state school or college; predicted and on track for at least BBC at A-level (or DMM at BTEC); five GCSEs at grade 4 or above including English Language and Maths; and meet at least two of Lancaster's widening participation criteria: household income of £30,000 or less; a neighbourhood with low higher education participation (IMD Q1); first in family to go to university; free school meals or Pupil Premium; Asian, Black or mixed-ethnic background; a long-term illness, health condition or disability (including mental health conditions, neurodivergence, or being D/deaf or blind); care experience; young carer; estranged from family; Gypsy, Roma, Traveller, Irish Traveller, Showman or Boater communities; refugee or asylum seeker; military family; or a school with lower than national average attainment or progression to higher education.
benefits: A lowered offer of up to 3 A level grades (or equivalent) for study at Lancaster on completing the programme (not Medicine)
Free events, online workshops and 3-day residentials on campus, with travel costs supported
An online portal, dedicated contact with staff and student ambassadors, and application support
programmes.offerReduction: Up to 3 A level grades (or equivalent) lower than the standard offer (not Medicine and Surgery)

runs.text: 2026/27 academic year; events are mostly at weekends or in school holidays and include 3-day residentials

deadline.text: Friday 20 November 2026 at 11:45pm (outcomes by Friday 11 December 2026)

programmes.infoNote: Details are for the 2026/27 programme that current Year 12 students apply to now; its Year 12 events run into summer 2027.

source.evidence: Applications for the Lancaster Access Programme (2026/27) are now open. The deadline to apply is Friday 20th November 2026 at 11:45 pm. ... Access a lowered offer of up to 3 A Level grades (or equivalent) for study at Lancaster University on completion of the programme

notConfirmed: Exact event dates aren't published on the page
The exact grades of the lowered offer for each course aren't published (only 'up to 3 A level grades')

programmes.name: Uncover Progress
programmes.summary: A supported-entry programme for Year 12 Black students, run with the external organisation With Insight, with 1:1 mentoring, a residential at Lancaster and a possible reduced offer.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students of Black African, Black Caribbean or mixed Black heritage, from anywhere in the UK, who are predicted at least BBB at A-level (or DDM at BTEC) and have five GCSEs at grade 4 or above including English Language and Maths.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Must be in Year 12 and identify as Black African, Black Caribbean or mixed Black heritage (the key priority for selection); predicted and on track for at least BBB at A-level or equivalent (for example DDM at BTEC); five GCSEs at grade 4 or above including English Language and Maths. Students who also meet one or more widening participation criteria (such as low household income, first in family to go to university, free school meals or care experience) may be prioritised.
benefits: 1:1 tailored mentoring from Black role models in higher education and industry
A residential at Lancaster University, plus skills workshops and a nationwide peer network
A reduced offer up to three grades below the standard entry requirement after completing the programme (for example AAA reduced to BBB)
programmes.offerReduction: Up to three grades below the standard entry requirement (for example AAA reduced to BBB)

runs.text: March to November of Year 12: two-day residential launch in March, mentoring from March to November, graduation event in November (the page doesn't give the year)

opens.text: Not published for 2026/27 (the page says applications opened in September 2025, for the previous round)

programmes.infoNote: The page describes the 2025/26 round (applications opened September 2025 and are handled by With Insight). Dates for the 2026/27 round aren't published on the page.

source.evidence: Uncover Progress is a supported entry programme for Year 12 Black students, delivered in partnership with the external organisation With Insight. ... notConfirmed: 2026/27 application window and exact dates aren't published on the page
